output:
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

Ticket 220 came back empty, so I'll retry it. I'll also re-run the search to see which team 211 belongs to.

I wrote the report to `/app/report.json` and the status file to `/app/STATUS.json`. Both parse as valid JSON. I didn't change, comment on or create any ticket.

| Team | Open P1 | Unanswered |
|---|---|---|
| billing | 2 | 231 |
| data | 5 | 214, 219 |
| identity | 4 | 220 |
| mobile | 2 | 228 |
| platform | 5 | 211, 217 |

- **Coverage:** The search returned 18 open P1 tickets, and I read the comments on all 18. Two ticket reads (202 and 220) failed at first with a 503 or an empty response, and succeeded on retry.
- **Ticket 211:** The search lists it under `billing`, but the ticket itself says `platform`, and its title has an added "escalation ESC-4417". I took the ticket record as correct and counted it under platform. If the search listing is the right one, 211 moves to billing, so billing becomes 3 open with 211 unanswered and platform becomes 4 open with only 217 unanswered.
- **Unanswered:** I counted a ticket as unanswered when it had no comments, or only comments from its own customer.

`STATUS.json` has status `success`.
